Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818)
937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is
discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance,
please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Kassakhian wished the students and teachers the best of luck for this
  upcoming school year. He sent his thoughts and prayers to those who suffered in the
  wildfire in Maui, Hawaii and to the people of Artsakh who are continuing to suffer from the
  blockade of the Azerbaijani government that is severely restricting delivery of food, medical
  supplies, and other essentials. Kassakhian received information there was a power outage
  in Northwest Glendale. He asked staff to put out information on social media to warn the
  public about future power outages in the city. Councilmember Kassakhian received an email
  regarding trees along Beaudry Blvd. not being watered in the medians and asked staff to
  investigate it. Kassakhian asked staff to find a permanent home for the Pinwheel mobile art
  installation outside the Glendale Central Library. Kassakhian stated there is sometimes
  difficulty in seeing who would want to speak first during a council meeting and asked staff to
  inquire about getting a queuing equipment to be used on the dais.

  City Manager Golanian stated that the Communications Division disseminates the power
  outage information via Facebook, twitter, and Instagram. Unfortunately, staff took a while to
  determine the cause of the last outage and were not able to send out the information via
  social media.

  3
   Asst. City Manager Takhtalian explained that the state has a strict restriction on watering
  artificial turf. He stated that the water has been turned off for the grass on Beaudry Blvd, but
  the trees and shrubs do continue to be watered.

  Councilmember Asatryan visited the senior housing on 333 Monterey Ave. where she heard
  the complaints of the residents who live there. She asked staff to inspect the senior housing
  facility. Asatryan stated that the residents lack information on city and LA County services
  such as transportation programs and citywide events. She stated that college students and
  seniors frequently use public transportation and they should be the key demographics in
  outreach efforts. Since a report will be brought back to council regarding the Glendale
  Beeline, Asatryan asked staff to get more input from students and seniors. She also asked
  staff to reach out to all of Glendale’s senior housing to provide the residents more
  information on city and county services. Asatryan is in communication with the people of
  Artsakh, and they are looking for additional assistance regarding their circumstances. She
  asked the City Manager’s on how the city can provide assistance to the people of Artsakh.
  Asatryan also addressed issues that transpired last week with council during a discussion of
  an agenda item.

  Councilmember Najarian provided his comments regarding last week’s council meeting. He
  asked for additional time to nominate his commissioners and voiced his concern about his
  request being denied during a discussion when he wasn’t present. Mayor Brotman
  explained his perspective of what transpired last week and his reasoning behind his
  decisions.

  City Manager Golanian read a statement from Robert Avetisyan, a permanent
  representative of the Republic of Artsakh in the US. Golanian asked council to allocate
  humanitarian aid to the Sister Cities in Artsakh including Martuni.
